t: Egypt's imperial age, founded when Ahmose I expelled the Hyksos c. 1550 BCE, stretched from Nubia to the Euphrates.
Nubian gold, Levantine tribute and the Amarna letters' great-power diplomacy made Egypt the hub of the Late Bronze Age world.
It ended not by conquest but by dissolution, as the Bronze Age Collapse and the rising Amun priesthood hollowed out royal power.
dyk: Ramesses II and the Hittites made peace in 1258 BCE in the earliest treaty to survive in both parties' versions, settling a stalemate after the Battle of Kadesh.
ev: Ahmose I completes the expulsion of the Hyksos and reunites Egypt
Thutmose III defeats a Canaanite coalition at Megiddo after a daring march through the Aruna pass
Akhenaten begins his reign, elevating the Aten and moving the capital to Akhetaten
Ramesses II fights the Hittite king Muwatalli II to a draw at the Battle of Kadesh
Egypt and the Hittites conclude a peace treaty acknowledging strategic stalemate
Ramesses III repels land and sea invasions by the Sea Peoples
Ramesses III is assassinated by harem conspirators
Death of Ramesses XI ends the New Kingdom amid administrative dissolution
